input.quote: “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property.
input.rationale: The Agreement has no indemnification article at all: the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "defend" return only clauses that presuppose an indemnity (Section 21.3 carving out "indemnification obligations" from the cap, Section 19.4 referring to "indemnified claims", Section 30.5 preserving "vested indemnity rights") plus Section 9.3's dangling cross-reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5". With no Vendor IP indemnity anywhere, the document sits in walk-away territory under this rule, so we inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary exclusions, and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (which also repairs the Section 20.5 cross-reference). No super-cap is needed because Section 21.3 already treats indemnity obligations as Excluded Claims.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 20 (Indemnification) with Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, narrow Customer indemnity, procedure, exclusions and infringement remedies
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity article even though Sections 9.3, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists (9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5"), so we have added the standard Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data incidents and wilful misconduct. We have kept Customer's reciprocal indemnity narrow and included the usual notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary exclusions and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from and against any third-party claim, and resulting damages, costs, and expenses, to the extent arising out of content or materials Customer provides to Vendor or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of a claim, provided that a delay relieves the indemnifying Party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced. The indemnifying Party shall control the defence with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. The indemnifying Party shall not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission of fault, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified Party without its prior written consent.

Vendor's obligations under Section 20.1(a) do not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or a Deliverable, combination of the Services or a Deliverable with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not have arisen absent the combination, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.

If a claim described in Section 20.1(a) is made or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with functionally equivalent non-infringing material. If neither remedy is commercially feasible, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated period and Fees paid for the affected Deliverable.
